motivation: After exact-point Thalassia loss, points retaining another seagrass were more likely to re-record Thalassia, but the within-node audit weakened that association. Test whether pre-loss focal persistence history itself carries recovery information, consistent with local meadow/clonal legacy or persistent microsite quality.

primary_population.sequence_rule: same frozen 259 three-year exact-point Thalassia-loss sequences from microsite_recovery_pathway_v1
primary_population.pre_loss_run_length: number of immediately consecutive consensus years ending in the source year with Thalassia recorded present at the same stable point; stop at first missing year or Thalassia-absent year; minimum=1
required_controls: loss-year vegetation state: other seagrass vs no seagrass

primary_hypothesis.statement: Within stable transects, longer-than-usual consecutive pre-loss Thalassia occupancy history is associated with higher one-year Thalassia re-recording after a one-year loss.
primary_hypothesis.predictor: pre_loss_run_length centered by stable-node mean among eligible sequences
primary_hypothesis.outcome: Thalassia recorded present at the same meter mark in the recovery year
primary_hypothesis.model: L2-regularized logistic regression with stable-node categorical effects and frozen controls; primary coefficient is the node-centered pre-loss run-length term
primary_hypothesis.uncertainty: stable-node bootstrap; refit the same model after resampling stable nodes with replacement
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for the centered run-length coefficient > 0

secondary_descriptive: distribution of pre-loss run length among return and non-return sequences
overall return fraction by integer run length where at least 10 sequences occur
same coefficient without node-centering, reported only as descriptive contrast

interpretation.supported: Longer local focal persistence history predicts re-recording after loss even after stable transect identity and community-continuity controls, consistent with a local legacy or residual-structure signal.
interpretation.unsupported: Pre-loss focal persistence history does not add robust within-transect recovery information beyond node identity and community state; broad site quality and current community continuity remain better-supported explanations.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc temporal ecology on an already-opened recovery endpoint.
A history effect would not distinguish residual rhizomes, clonal memory, persistent microsite habitat quality, or repeated detectability.
Re-recording is an observation-state return, not genet-level recolonization.
Do not change the run-length definition, node-centering, control set, regularization, bootstrap unit, minima, or support threshold after opening the history endpoint.
Do not infer a causal clonal-memory mechanism without direct below-ground measurements.
